title: Bottom shelf
description: These feeding vessels, despite differences in design over time, were made to support the needs of people. They represent difference, creating change in [material] culture.

audioDescription.transcript: A white porcelain cup, with a long pouring spout and small handle. The top of the cup is half- enclosed on the spout side to enable the vessel to be tilted. There is a gold decorative line applied to the top of the vessel, outlining the rim. A gold line also runs down the side of the spout to the point at which it meets the cup wall, and a gold line is also observed on the vessel’s handle. The faded nature of this line may indicate frequent use of this object.

images.altText: Object 10. Spouted vessel. A likely wheel-made ceramic vessel. There is a handle over the top of a flaring rim. The vessel has a narrow neck and a wide, ovoid-shaped body with a circular base.  At the shoulder of the vessel is a spout, pointed upwards to allow the vessel to tilt. Several faded black lines can be seen around the handle, neck, and body.
images.caption: 10. Spouted vessel, MU0091, front-angled view © Gale History Museum

audioDescription.transcript: A likely wheel-made ceramic vessel. There is a handle arching over a flaring rim. The vessel has a narrow neck and wide, ovoid-shaped body tapering to a small circular base.  At the shoulder of the vessel is a spout, pointed upwards at an acute angle to allow the vessel to tilt. Several faded black painted lines can be seen as decoration around the handle, neck, and body. The spout was likely originally painted black in colour, although the surface is now eroded in places. The painted lines around the neck are tightly arranged, with a thick black line at the neck base. A thick, faded, wavy line extends around the shoulder of the vessel at the level of the spout.
